l1.title: How much did each of these hurt?
l1.description: For each selected asset, how much it lost at the worst moments of the period: the bad day, the bad month, the deepest fall, and how far it still stands below its peak.

columnHelp.badDay: The average loss on the worst 5% of days in the window (historical CVaR at 95%).
columnHelp.badMonth: Like the bad day, over a longer run of consecutive days: the average loss on the worst 5% of those runs (historical CVaR at 95%).
columnHelp.worstFall: The deepest fall from a peak to the lowest point that followed it within the window, and how long it lasted.
columnHelp.currentFall: How far below its highest point in the window the asset stands on the last day.
columnHelp.toPeak: How much it must rise to get back to that highest point: after a 20% fall it takes +25%.

l3.title: What did each of these pay for its risk?
l3.description: For each selected asset, how much it swung and how much it returned on average per year, in the table and in the chart; with a benchmark chosen just above, also how much it moved along with it.

columnHelp.volatility: How much the asset's returns swing, on a yearly basis: the standard deviation of the period's returns, annualised.
columnHelp.expectedReturn: The average of the period's returns, scaled to a year by how often the asset is quoted. It describes the past, not a forecast. For a very volatile asset it is higher than what the asset actually returned, because swings erode the compounded return.
columnHelp.sortino: How much average annual return for each unit of downward swing: it looks at the falls only, not at the rises.
columnHelp.sharpe: How much average annual return for each unit of volatility: the pay for the risk taken, rises and falls alike.
columnHelp.beta: How much the asset moved when the benchmark moved: 1 means as much, 2 twice as much, 0 independently of it.
columnHelp.correlation: How closely the asset and the benchmark moved together, from −1 (always opposite) to +1 (always together).

period.annualized: Volatility and average return are annualised; Sharpe and Sortino derive from them.

l3.referenceItself: Not applicable: this asset is the benchmark itself, and it is not compared with itself.

simulation.assumptions: {paths} paths over {days} days; current buy-and-hold composition, without costs, cash flows, inflation or rebalancing.

block_bootstrap.label: Reshuffled history
block_bootstrap.hypothesis: Your own returns, reordered in blocks. No assumption is added.

calm.label: Calm market
calm.hypothesis: Assumption: your real swings, reduced by 30%. Correlations and direction stay those of your history.

prolonged_crisis.label: Prolonged crisis
prolonged_crisis.hypothesis: Assumption: swings ×2.5 and a −20% annual return for 14 months. Correlations stay those of your history.

shock_recovery.label: Shock and recovery
shock_recovery.hypothesis: Assumption: a 35% drop applied on top of your history over 2 months, then your real history resumes.

gbm.label: Normal curve (GBM)
gbm.hypothesis: Classic model: it assumes regular swings and underestimates the tails.
